title.en: The Beekeeping Pages of the Madrid Codex

region.en: Madrid Codex (Maya east coast tradition), symbolic pin at Cozumel
region.zh: 馬德里抄本（馬雅東岸傳統），以科蘇梅爾為象徵定位

source.work: Madrid (Tro-Cortesianus) Codex, pp. 103-112, in Schellhas (1904) and Villacorta & Villacorta, Codices Mayas (1933)

summary.en: Ten pages of the Madrid Codex are given to the bees: the bee-god appears among hives, honey is offered, gods tend the stingless hives of Yucatan, and rites for the swarms are prescribed — the codex keeps a liturgy of beekeeping, the one surviving Maya book of agricultural ceremony.
summary.zh: 馬德里抄本十頁皆記蜂事：蜂神現於蜂巢之間，蜂蜜獻祭，諸神照管猶加敦的無刺蜂群，並為蜂群規定祭儀——抄本中竟存有一部養蜂禮書，即碩果僅存的馬雅農事經典。

passages.text: In Codex Tro-Cortesianus, pp. 103-112, there is a long portion which has to do with the bees. The god of the bees is pictured among the hives; there is a rite, probably an offering of corn in some form in honor of the bee god, and the figures handle the stingless hives of Yucatan as objects of ceremony.
passages.note: Condensed from Schellhas (1904) and Tozzer (1907), on the beekeeping pages; not verbatim.

passages.text: A mythologic significance also seems to belong to the bee which plays so prominent a part in the Madrid manuscript; the gods of the wild bees of the four quarters appear in the Dresden Codex with their flowers for cups — the red bees of the east, the white of the north, the black of the west, the yellow of the south.
passages.note: Condensed from Schellhas (1904) and the Chumayel ritual of the four world-quarters; not verbatim.

region.en: Madrid Codex, symbolic pin at Cozumel
region.zh: 馬德里抄本，以科蘇梅爾為象徵定位

summary.en: In the Madrid manuscript the goddess distinguished by symbols of flood and water appears; she is doubtless the same as goddess I of the Dresden Codex — the water-goddess invariably marked by the serpent on her head, the symbol of the water flowing along and forming waves, bringing the evil days with her.
summary.zh: 馬德里抄本中以洪水與水之符號為標記的女神出現；她無疑即德累斯頓抄本的女神I——頭戴蛇結的水神，蛇即流淌成波之水的符號，伴隨凶日而來。

passages.text: The goddess distinguished in the Madrid manuscript by symbols of flood and water is doubtless the same as goddess I of the Dresden manuscript described above; her unmistakable character of water-goddess in both manuscripts is in favor of this. In both manuscripts she is invariably distinguished by the serpent on her head, which is a symbol of the water flowing along and forming waves.
passages.note: Condensed from Schellhas (1904), on Goddess I in the Madrid Codex; not verbatim.

passages.text: The figure corresponding to her in the Madrid manuscript, in Troano 27 and 34c, displays some variations, in particular the tiger claws on the feet and the red-brown color of the body are lacking; but the agreement cannot be questioned when we recall that the Maya manuscripts doubtless originated in different ages and different areas of civilization.

title.en: The Paris Codex: The Cycle of the Thirteen Katuns
title.zh: 巴黎抄本：十三卡特倫之週期

region.en: Paris Codex (Yucatec), symbolic pin at Chichen Itza
region.zh: 巴黎抄本（猶加敦），以奇琴伊察為象徵定位

source.work: Paris Codex (Perez Codex), katun cycle, in Schellhas (1904) and Villacorta & Villacorta, Codices Mayas (1933)

summary.en: The Paris Codex preserves the cycle of the thirteen katuns — the prophetic wheel by which each twenty-year period has its lord, its omen, and its end: the Maya zodiac and the katun prophecies that would later be written out in the Books of Chilam Balam.
summary.zh: 巴黎抄本保存了十三卡特倫之週期——預言的輪盤，每個二十年各有其主、其兆與其終：即馬雅黃道帶，也就是後來寫入《奇拉姆·巴拉姆之書》的卡特倫預言。

passages.text: The Paris manuscript preserves the cycle of the thirteen katuns, the count in which each katun of twenty years is ruled by its own lord and carries its own prophecy. The wheel of the katuns is the Maya zodiac: figures of the katun lords with their dates and their omens, the frame into which the Books of Chilam Balam pour their histories.
passages.note: Condensed from Schellhas (1904) and standard descriptions of the Paris Codex katun cycle; not verbatim.

passages.text: With the katun cycle the Paris Codex gives the divisions of the sky and the creatures set in them; Spinden suggested that the Maya zodiac is shown in its pages — the serpent, the birds, and the monsters that carry the years.
passages.note: Condensed from Schellhas (1904) and Spinden's suggestion on the Maya zodiac; not verbatim.
